findings.F1: The test's main measure is on the predicted side but short of the bar: the forecast-weighted excess 2-day return after Sunday drops has t 1.35 over 1197 cases (my recount: t 1.30, n 1196), and the top-minus-bottom-third check passes (+0.0025). The six coins all have positive per-coin means but per-coin t only 0.04 to 1.44, so the sign is consistent and the size is too small for these six coins.
findings.F2: The plain rebound exists but is weakly graded. Sunday drops are followed by a mean excess 2-day return of +0.0065 (t 2.84, n 967), against +0.00044 after weekday drops (Welch t, Sunday minus weekday, 2.46). Yet the deepest quartile of drops rebounds less (+0.0047, t 0.90) than the second and third quartiles (+0.0113 and +0.0101, t 2.64 and 2.20). The depth-weighted product therefore reaches only t 1.53, and the grading the plan rewards is what dilutes it.
findings.F3: The effect sits mostly in certain years. The main measure has t 4.07 in 2020 (n 156) and 1.43 in 2021, against -2.81 in 2018 (n 143), and it is near zero (t between -0.13 and 0.63) in 2019 and 2022–2025.
findings.F4: The horizon matters. Product t for Sunday drops is 2.68 at 1 day and 2.52 at 3 days, against 1.53 at the plan's 2 days.
findings.F5: The opposite side shows more clearly. Sunday rises are followed by a mean excess 2-day return of -0.0098 (t -4.26, n 1083). Across all Sundays, the slope of excess 2-day return on the Sunday move in usual moves is -0.0046 (t -2.46). No other weekday has a 2-day slope with |t| above 1.6.
findings.F6: More data is available. Thirteen more coins (ADA, DOGE, LINK, TRX, UNI, AAVE, AVAX, SOL, INJ, NEAR, SUI, TAO, ONDO) have folds A and D, plus parts of B and C. This could multiply the 1197 cases, which is what a positive t of 1.35 needs.

ideas.name: weekend drop rebound, more coins
ideas.idea: A coin that fell over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) rises over the next 2 days (Monday and Tuesday), and the larger the weekend drop, the larger the rebound.
ideas.consequence: Weekend drops are partly undone once weekday liquidity returns.

ideas.idea: A coin that rose over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) falls over the next 2 days (Monday and Tuesday), and the larger the weekend rise, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: Weekend rallies are partly given back once weekday liquidity returns, which is a reason to refuse chasing them on Monday or to lean short against them.
ideas.name: weekend rise fades Monday
